sidebar.text: This page covers the essentials. For the complete Code of Studies and Exams, subject description requirements, and other academic regulations, see the Rules and Regulations page of the Academic Services Centre (ASC/KTH).

items.text: Unless stated otherwise, the preliminary subject and course registration period starts at 18:00 on the third working day after the exam period and ends at 12:00 on the last working day before the registration week. The final course registration period starts at 18:00 on the first day of the registration week and runs until 23:59 on the last day of that week.

For exact dates and times, students should always check the official ASC website. You can also always find all the dates on the websites, Instagram and Facebook of the Students' Union or Faculty Student Councils.
It's possible to register for or drop a subject after the regular period, but only until the first day of the second teaching week. You must submit a request via Neptun:
items: Request 018 – Subject registration/withdrawal request (not your own fault)
Request 019 – Late subject registration/withdrawal request (your own fault) — a 5,500 HUF fee per subject applies if it's your own fault.

blocks.text: Each semester (both fall and spring) is divided into 4 parts:

items.text: Registration week (3–5 workdays) — this is when you need to set your semester to active and decide which classes you want to take. It's important to check whether you have any payments left to cover, as any overdue payment will prevent you from registering to any classes.

Active semester period (at least 14 weeks, but at most 70 workdays) — the main part of the semester, where students attend classes, midterm tests are written, and assignments are made. Exam registration is also scheduled for the 14th week.
Retake week (5 days) — most test retakes and late assignment submissions happen this week. There might also be a possibility to take an early exam, depending on the subject.

Exam period (20 workdays) — before the exam period, you need to register for exams, which is also prevented if you have late payments left. Exams can be retaken as many times as possible if there are exam times and student spaces left in the semester; however, from the second retake of an exam (3rd time), it will cost a fee.

blocks.text: If problems occur during your studies, you should contact your professor if:

items.text: You have problems with your homework
You couldn't attend a laboratory class and have to go to another

blocks.text: You should contact the Students' Council of your Faculty if:

items.text: The whole class has the same problem
Over 50% fail on a test or exam
You don't understand something about the CoS (Code of Studies and Exams)

blocks.text: Most study-related and administrative matters at BME are handled through requests submitted in Neptun (Administration → Requests). For the full, up-to-date list of available requests — including tuition, subject registration, certificates, and more — see the Academic Services Centre's official list.

TDK (Students' Scientific Association) is a chance to dive into a topic you love, do real research, and present your findings at a university conference. You'll work with a lecturer (your advisor) and write a paper, then present it in November at BME's TDK Conference.

items: University students with an advisor and a specific topic; high school students interested in research.
Pick a topic that fascinates you, find a lecturer to be your advisor, and start working in spring or early summer.
September – apply with your topic, advisor, and summary.
November – submit your paper and give your presentation. The best projects move on to the national OTDK round.

blocks.text: Check your faculty's TDK page for deadlines and topic ideas.
